results.name: set_level_yes_rate_sd
results.description: Standard deviation across sets (with >=3 distinct targets) of each set's mean yes-rate; observed > null means people's overall willingness to say yes varies by set more than the model's single bias/slope mapping from summed similarity produces (set-specific rule breadth).
results.code:
# name: set_level_yes_rate_sd
# description: Standard deviation across sets (with >=3 distinct targets) of each set's mean yes-rate; observed > null means people's overall willingness to say yes varies by set more than the model's single bias/slope mapping from summed similarity produces (set-specific rule breadth).

def _feats(df):
    # per unique (set, target) pair features; loops only over unique pairs
    pairs = df[["number_set", "target"]].drop_duplicates()
    rows = []
    for s, t in zip(pairs["number_set"].values, pairs["target"].values):
        ex = [int(x) for x in str(s).split(",")]
        t = int(t)
        d = [abs(t - e) for e in ex]
        par = set(e % 2 for e in ex)
        digs = [e % 10 for e in ex]
        nearest = ex[int(np.argmin(d))]
        rows.append(dict(number_set=s, target=t, n=len(ex), mind=min(d),
                         dmatch=float(t % 10 in digs),
                         singlepar=float(len(par) == 1),
                         samepar=float(len(par) == 1 and t % 2 in par),
                         nearsamepar=float(nearest % 2 == t % 2),
                         digit_homog=float(len(ex) >= 2 and len(set(digs)) == 1),
                         all3odd=float(all(e % 3 == 0 and e % 2 == 1 for e in ex) and len(ex) >= 2),
                         inrange=float(min(ex) < t < max(ex))))
    f = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    f["target"] = f["target"].astype(int)
    d2 = df[["number_set", "target", "rating"]].copy()
    d2["target"] = d2["target"].astype(int)
    return d2.merge(f, on=["number_set", "target"], how="left")

def _rate(x):
    return float(x["rating"].mean()) if len(x) else 0.0


def test_statistic(df):
    f = _feats(df)
    nt = f.groupby("number_set")["target"].nunique()
    keep = nt[nt >= 3].index
    g = f[f["number_set"].isin(keep)].groupby("number_set")["rating"].mean()
    return float(g.std(ddof=0)) if len(g) > 1 else 0.0

results.name: digit_homog_near_nomatch_rate

results.name: parity_contrast_near_nodigit
results.description: In single-parity sets (>=2 examples), yes-rate for same-parity minus opposite-parity targets that lie within 10 of some example and share no final digit with any example; observed > null means people reject near opposite-parity targets more sharply (rule-like parity) than the model's constant multiplicative parity penalty predicts, observed < null means parity matters less near the examples than the model assumes.

results.name: inrange_vs_outside_far_nodigit

results.name: multiple7_contrast_nodigit
results.description: For sets whose examples are all multiples of 7 (28,98; 7,63; 84,56), yes-rate for targets that are multiples of 7 minus non-multiples, among targets more than 5 from every example and sharing no final digit with any example; observed > null means people induce a multiples-of-7 rule the similarity model cannot represent.

    return float(x["rating"].mean()) if len(x) else 0.0


def test_statistic(df):

results.name: mixed_set_nearest_parity_contrast

results.name: far_target_magnitude_slope
results.description: Correlation between target value and yes response among targets more than 10 from every example and sharing no final digit with any example; observed < null means people favour small numbers (a magnitude prior), observed > null means they favour large ones, beyond what similarity to the examples predicts.
